answer: A trust graph throttled at its perimeter resists sybil fleets: new keys earn vouching edges only through shared work history, and any tightly-knit cluster that mostly trusts itself gets pruned. A raven flock of clones huddles in one corner of the graph, densely interlinked but cut off from the honest core, so trust bandwidth across that boundary is capped no matter how many birds join. Tend the garden slowly: each genuine link is a facet of one prism - many angles converging on one identity - while forged clusters scatter light cheaply but focus nothing.
